item.title: Bobo’s: Beryl Stafford. A Single Mom Turns a Baking Project into a $100M Business
item.description: Bobo’s: Beryl Stafford. A Single Mom Turns a Baking Project into a $100M BusinessAt 40, Beryl Stafford’s life cracked open. Her marriage ended, she hadn’t worked in years, and she had two daughters to raise. She needed income—fast. So she did the only thing that felt real: she baked.What started as 4-ingredient oat bars— hastily placed in a Boulder coffee shop—became Bobo’s, a national brand built in the Silicon Valley of natural foods. item.title: You're healthier than they say you are. Here's why.
item.description: Are Americans actually becoming less healthy?That’s an idea that Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been repeating for a while now. While there are some nuggets of truth in that – on the whole, American life expectancy has gone up a lot in Kennedy’s lifetime. So why does a backward-looking narrative serve his agenda? And what would actually move the needle forward on improving Americans’ health?Brittany is joined by NPR health policy correspondent Selena Simmons-Duffin

item.title: Sérgio & Odair Assad at 92NY
item.description: Sérgio & Odair Assad at 92NYMar. 14. 7:30PM. $45+up In the 1980s, the Brazilian guitar duo of Sérgio & Odair Assad released an album of music by Argentine tango composer Astor Piazzolla. Within a few years, the Assad Brothers were the most sought-after guitar duo in the world. They’ve won Grammys, played with leading classical musicians like Yo-Yo Ma, and greatly expanded the repertoire for two guitars. Now, Sérgio & Odair Assad are bidding farewell, with their final concert on Saturday, March 1
